scope: Authored fixture wrapper exception path during an externally signalled operator cancellation after an actual protected availability request. This is separate from prior standalone interpreter and external repository bounded-cleanup v3 coverage.

scenario.cancellationTrigger: AbortSignal raised 50 ms after the actual browser availability request; the request is held by the authored adapter.

versions.versionEvidence: Wrapper identifiers are from inspected source. The before harness returned no execution receipt; manual after harness logged status but not versions. Final targeted tests explicitly assert wrapper v3 identity.

before.recordingMethod: Transcribed actual pre-fix reproduction observation from this worker session; the original stdout was not saved as a file. The harness closed the leaked browser in its own finally block after observing it connected.

result.error: Error: Synthetic review cancellation during actual availability

after.recordingMethod: Exact fields transcribed from the actual post-fix reproduction stdout, before the final wrapper-only identity bump from v2 to v3; no new reproduction was run for this documentation.

change: The wrapper starts context/browser close independently of recorder.stop or gate disposal, waits at most 2000 ms for teardown, and retains an already-produced cancelled execution when recorder stop rejects because of the same abort. Shutdown failures never establish success.

verification.command: npx vitest run tests/temporal-fixture-cancel.test.ts && npx tsc --noEmit
tests: Actual pending availability cancellation returns a cancelled execution with request trace and no protected booking; launched browser is disconnected.
Normal baseline passes all checks, creates the expected protected appointment and closes its browser.

localEvidence.limitation: Local /tmp evidence is not a durable public artifact. This public record preserves the observations and current source hashes; transcript files are not represented as original raw stdout.

focusedReductionHistoryReview.method: Read-only inspection of current scheduler, service export/error path, shared metadata and UI; no additional browser or integration run.
observations: Scheduler retains each completed replay before checking cancellation and throwing; inconclusive error/cancelled trials cannot establish local minimality.
Service appends completed/error runs and replay IDs; an errored run updates the existing counterexample historyCount transactionally.
Legacy counts-only records remain distinct, with missing original timestamps/rejected traces disclosed. Export includes starts, runs and replays.
UI shows bounded or locally reduced counterexamples, actual action/removal/replay counts, retained history and explicit search limitation; no global minimum claim.
focusedReductionHistoryReview.limitations: A latest counterexample is a view of its last completed reduction. Errored/partial subsequent runs remain in export history. Identical candidate schedules may reuse observations; cached evidence does not establish nondeterministic behavior.

limitations: Automated synthetic fixture QA, not human participant or independent accessibility acceptance.
The authored adapter and generic interpreter have separate identities. Prior interpreter/external v3 records do not exercise this authored wrapper cancellation exception path.
When no completed execution is safely available, the wrapper propagates the original error after requesting closure.
Browser termination is requested and the cleanup wait is bounded; this API does not guarantee OS-level forced process exit within 2000 ms.
Historical receipts are unchanged. Final portable authored replay is a separate root-owned validation.
